## Overview

A badge is a small, non-interactive marker attached to something else. It comes in three types:

- **Count** shows how many new or unread items wait behind a tab, an icon or a row: "3", "99+".
- **Dot** says that something is new without saying how much.
- **Text** is a short status or promotional tag beside content: "New", "Sale", "Sold out", "Free cancellation".

A badge never takes focus and never does anything when tapped. Whatever it is attached to carries the interaction.

Four variant axes drive it:

- **Type**: Count, Text, Dot.
- **Emphasis**:
  - **Strong** is a solid fill with white text. It is the default for counts and the only option for dots.
  - **Subtle** is a tinted fill with coloured text, the calm option for status tags that sit next to content.
- **Intent** follows the Cosmos semantic naming:

  | Intent | Colour | Used for |
  |---|---|---|
  | Neutral | near black / grey | no status |
  | Brand | blue | promotions |
  | Info | blue | information |
  | Success | green | positive status |
  | Caution | amber | advisory |
  | Warning | red | unread counts and errors |

- **Size**:
  - **Small** is 16 tall with 12/16 type, for tabs, icons and dense rows.
  - **Medium** is 24 tall with 14/20 type, for cards and beside headings.

A Dot has no Subtle emphasis. A pale dot is too faint to see against the page, below the 3:1 non-text contrast minimum.

### When to use something else

| Situation | Use |
|---|---|
| The marker is tappable, filters a list or can be removed | Chip |
| The message is a sentence or needs an action | Snackbar or an inline banner |
| The status belongs to a whole card or page section | A banner or a coloured surface |
| A rating, a price or a date | Plain text in the layout, not a badge |

### Composition

- A Count or Text badge is one text layer inside a pill or rounded frame. A Dot is an empty filled frame.
- **Icon / bell** (`685:28`, Material Symbols Rounded `notifications`, weight 300) was added to the Icons page (`645:2`) for the examples. It is not part of the component.
- There are no nested components and no icons. An icon inside a text badge is a known gap.

## API

| Property | Type | Values | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | enum | count \| text \| dot | `count` | Maps to Figma `Type`. |
| `count` | number | (number) | – | Used when `type=count`. Above 99 it renders as "99+", and a count of 0 hides the badge (see Behaviour). |
| `max` | number | (number) | `99` | The largest count shown before the "+" suffix. |
| `label` | string | (string) | – | Used when `type=text`. One or two words. |
| `intent` | enum | neutral \| brand \| info \| success \| caution \| warning | `warning` for count and dot, `neutral` for text | Maps to Figma `Intent`. |
| `emphasis` | enum | strong \| subtle | `strong` | Maps to Figma `Emphasis`. Ignored for `type=dot`, which is always strong. |
| `size` | enum | small \| medium | `small` | Maps to Figma `Size`. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | string | (string) | derived | What a screen reader says. Defaults to "{count} new" for a count and "New" for a dot. See Accessibility. |

### Figma-only properties

| Figma property | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Count` | TEXT | `"3"` | On the Count layer only. Placeholder copy. |
| `Label` | TEXT | `"Label"` | On the Text layer only. Placeholder copy. |

Count and Label are separate properties so that neither type resets the default of the other. The default variant, top left in the grid, is Count, Strong, Neutral, Small. Every variant ships placeholder copy only. Realistic copy lives in the `Badge examples` frame.

### Examples

| # | Configuration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `type=count`, `count=3`, `intent=warning`, `size=small` on a bell icon | Unread notifications. |
| 2 | `type=dot`, `intent=warning` on a tab | Something new, with no count. |
| 3 | `type=text`, `label="New"`, `intent=brand`, `emphasis=strong`, `size=medium` | A new product on a card. |
| 4 | `type=text`, `label="Free cancellation"`, `intent=success`, `emphasis=subtle` | A reassuring fare condition. |
| 5 | `type=text`, `label="Sold out"`, `intent=neutral`, `emphasis=subtle` | Status with no tone of alarm. |
| 6 | `type=count`, `count=128`, `intent=neutral`, `emphasis=subtle` | A long result count, shown as "99+". |

The Figma page has a live `Badge examples` frame (`686:177`) with counts on the `Icon / bell` glyph and text badges on two hotel cards.

## Behaviour

- **Counts.**

  | Value | Renders as |
  |---|---|
  | Greater than `max` | "{max}+", so 128 shows as "99+" |
  | 0 | hidden. A zero badge is noise. |
  | Negative | not a valid count |

  Format the number for the locale.
- **Text copy.**
  - Use one or two words in sentence case: "New", "Free cancellation".
  - Text badges do not wrap or truncate, so keep them short enough to fit beside their content on a 360 px screen.
- **Placement.**
  - Inline badges sit after their label with a gap set by the host component, for example `tab/secondary-gap-badge`.
  - Badges on an icon are pinned to its top-right corner: the badge left edge sits 16 px in from the icon left edge and its top 4 px above the icon top, and the badge grows to the right. On a 24 px icon a count overhangs the corner by 8 px right and 4 px up, and a dot straddles the corner. Tab / Primary tokenises this as `tab/primary-badge-offset-x` and `tab/primary-badge-offset-y`. Other hosts reuse the same rule until a shared overlay token exists (see Known gaps).
- **Change.** When a count changes, update it in place. Do not animate it, and do not move it.

## Structure

### Anatomy

```text
Badge (component set · 683:2823)
├─ Type=Count · horizontal auto layout · hug width, fixed height · centred · Small: bottom padding padding-bottom-sm
│  └─ Count (text · label/small/bold or label/medium/bold)
├─ Type=Text · the same frame with radius-text
│  └─ Label (text · label/small/bold or label/medium/bold)
└─ Type=Dot · fixed square frame, no children
```

### Dimensions

| Property | Small | Medium | Token |
|---|---|---|---|
| Height (Count, Text) | 16 | 24 | `badge/height-sm`, `badge/height-md` |
| Min width (Count, Text) | 16 | 24 | `badge/min-width-sm`, `badge/min-width-md` |
| Padding left and right, Count | 4 | 4 | `badge/padding-x-count` |
| Padding left and right, Text | 4 | 8 | `badge/padding-x-text-sm`, `badge/padding-x-text-md` |
| Padding top / bottom (Count, Text) | 0 / 2 | 0 / 0 | `badge/padding-bottom-sm` |
| Type | 12 / 16 bold | 14 / 20 bold | `label/small/bold`, `label/medium/bold` |
| Dot | 8 × 8 | 12 × 12 | `badge/dot-size-sm`, `badge/dot-size-md` |
| Radius (Count, Dot) | pill | pill | `badge/radius` |
| Radius (Text) | 4 | 4 | `badge/radius-text` |

Min width equals height, so a one-digit count is a perfect circle. Count padding is 4 at both sizes: at 8, a medium "3" would come out 25 wide and turn oval. Padding only shows once the content is wider than the circle, so "12" and "99+" stretch into a pill. Text badges get 8 at Medium so a tag beside a card title does not look cramped.

**Optical centring.** Lato places its capitals low in a line box. In a 16 px box at 12 px, the glyphs sit about 0.65 px below centre: 4.2 px of space above them and 2.9 px below. Small badges therefore take 2 px of bottom padding and no top padding. The 16 px line box stays in the 14 px content area and is centred, so the label rises 1 px, and its ink ends about 0.3 px above geometric centre, which reads as centred. Medium badges measure within 0.15 px of centre, so they need no offset. In code, keep the fixed height and centre alignment, and correct with bottom padding. Do not trim the text box or change the line height instead, because that detaches the text style in Figma and changes the metrics on each platform.

**On the web the padding differs from Figma.** Browsers round the ascent and descent of Lato to whole pixels, and Figma does not, so the same box puts the baseline half a pixel off: too high at Small and too low at Medium. Use 1 px of bottom padding at both sizes (half of `badge/padding-bottom-sm`). Measured in Chrome against the glyph bounds of the Figma variants, the ink then matches Figma exactly: 3.23 to 12.1 px in the Small box and 6.77 to 17.11 px in the Medium box. Check iOS and Android against the Figma glyph bounds in the same way, because their text engines place the baseline differently again.

The medium dot is 12 rather than 10. There is no 10 px step in the semantic space scale, and component tokens may not point at primitives.

## Color

Token names follow `badge/{property}-{emphasis}-{intent}`. Dots use `badge/dot-{intent}`.

| Intent | Strong fill / label | Subtle fill / label | Dot |
|---|---|---|---|
| Neutral | `bg-fill-inverse` #0A0A0A / `text-inverse` #FFFFFF | `bg-fill-secondary` #F5F5F5 / `text-secondary` #525252 | #0A0A0A |
| Brand | `bg-fill-brand` #0088FF / `text-brand-on-bg-fill` #FFFFFF | `bg-surface-brand` #EDFAFF / `text-brand` #0088FF | #0088FF |
| Info | `bg-fill-info-strong` #0088FF / `text-info-on-bg-fill-strong` #FFFFFF | `bg-fill-info-subtle` #EDFAFF / `text-info-on-bg-fill-subtle` #0088FF | #0088FF |
| Success | `bg-fill-success-strong` #008236 / `text-success-on-bg-fill-strong` #FFFFFF | `bg-fill-success-subtle` #DCFCE7 / `text-success-on-bg-fill-subtle` #008236 | #008236 |
| Caution | `bg-fill-caution-strong` #A65F00 / `text-caution-on-bg-fill-strong` #FFFFFF | `bg-fill-caution-subtle` #FEF9C2 / `text-caution-on-bg-fill-subtle` #894B00 | #A65F00 |
| Warning | `bg-fill-warning-strong` #C10007 / `text-warning-on-bg-fill-strong` #FFFFFF | `bg-fill-warning-subtle` #FFE2E2 / `text-warning-on-bg-fill-subtle` #C10007 | #C10007 |

Each `dot-*` token has the same value as its `bg-strong-*` token. It is a separate token so the `tokens/contrast` lint checks the dot against both page canvases at 3:1, which a fill behind text is not checked for.

This component adds no semantic roles.

## Accessibility

### Contrast

| Pair | Ratio | Required | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Strong label on strong fill, brand and info (#FFFFFF on #0088FF) | 3.52:1 | 3:1 (azure exception) | Pass |
| Strong label on strong fill, lowest outside azure (caution: #FFFFFF on #A65F00) | 4.93:1 | 4.5:1 (1.4.3) | Pass |
| Subtle label on subtle fill, brand and info (#0088FF on #EDFAFF) | 3.30:1 | 3:1 (azure exception) | Pass |
| Subtle label on subtle fill, lowest outside azure (success: #008236 on #DCFCE7) | 4.50:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Subtle neutral label #525252 on #F5F5F5 | 7.17:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Dot on white, lowest (brand and info #0088FF) | 3.52:1 | 3:1 (1.4.11) | Pass |
| Dot on grey #F5F5F5, lowest (brand and info #0088FF) | 3.22:1 | 3:1 | Pass |

A subtle fill against the page reaches only 1.0 to 1.2:1. That is fine: a text badge is identified by its words, not by its edge, so 1.4.11 does not apply to the fill. On the grey `bg-secondary` canvas, the Subtle Neutral fill matches the page exactly, and the badge reads as coloured text.

### Colour is never the only signal

- Intent colour adds meaning. It must not carry it alone, so a text badge says its status in words ("Payment failed", not a red "!").
- A dot has no words, so its host must expose the meaning to assistive technology (see Semantics).

### Semantics

A badge is not focusable and has no role of its own. Its text becomes part of the accessible name of the thing it is attached to.

| | Web | iOS / VoiceOver | Android / TalkBack |
|---|---|---|---|
| Count on a control | Append to the control name: `aria-label="Notifications, 3 new"`. Hide the visual badge with `aria-hidden="true"`. | Combine into the host element: `.accessibilityLabel("Notifications")` and `.accessibilityValue("3 new")`. | Merge into the host `contentDescription` ("Notifications, 3 new"), or set `stateDescription`. |
| Dot | Append "new" to the host name. | `accessibilityValue("New")` | `stateDescription = "New"` |
| Text badge | Real text in reading order after the content it tags. For a tag that is purely visual decoration, hide it and put the words in the host name. | Static text, combined with its card | Merged into its card |
| Changing count | If the change matters, announce it through the page live region. The badge itself is not a live region. | Post an announcement only for user-relevant changes | Same |

## Platform mapping

| | Android | iOS | Web |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base | A custom `Badge` composable. Material 3 `Badge` inside `BadgedBox` gives the icon overlay, with Cosmos colours and sizes. | A custom `Badge` view (a `Text` in a `Capsule`), with `.overlay(alignment: .topTrailing)` for icons | A `<span>` component, `inline-flex`, `aria-hidden` when the host names it |
| Count overflow | Format in the component using `max` | Same | Same |

## Known gaps

- **Brand and Info look identical.** Both resolve to #0088FF (strong) and #EDFAFF (subtle) today, because Cosmos info uses the brand hue. Both intents ship because their meaning differs, and they separate if either semantic role changes.
- **No shared icon overlay tokens.** Only Tab / Primary tokenises the offset of a badge over an icon corner (`tab/primary-badge-offset-x`, `tab/primary-badge-offset-y`). A shared badge-level offset, and an outline ring that separates the badge from a busy icon or an avatar, are not tokenised.
- **No leading icon in text badges**, such as a bolt beside "Deal".
- **No dark mode.** All variable collections are single-mode.
- **Not uSpec-generated.** This file is hand-authored next to the Figma build.
